items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Quincy of course we did things for him that were often more interesting than some of the other people.

ctx.x: Quincy would come to town now and then, yes. Quincy of course we did things for him that were often more interesting than some of the other people. They had more jazz content. Quincy actually worked often with the man who scored his ideas who was the actual arranger, well depending on how you defined it, and that was Billy Byers. Sometimes you know there’s a division of labor, especially in California. The composer will do a score up to a certain point and then an orchestrator will take over. And Billy it
was said did that sort of thing for Quincy. Let me see if I can think of some other arrangers. They’ll all come to me after we finish.
